conformance_note: This report was emitted by `ascep bench` and graded afterwards. A load generator observes latency and throughput over HTTP and nothing else, so the four report sections it cannot observe -- the roofline comparison, the sizing result, the scaling table, and the theoretical and recommended capacity tiers -- are left unknown rather than estimated, and they are why the grade is what it is. The claim below was written by `ascep conformance` from the findings it computed; running that command again on this file reproduces the grade.

hardware.interconnect_intra_node_u_reason: (U) TP=1 on a single GPU; there is no inter-GPU link in the serving path, so no intra-node interconnect was exercised and none is declared. Describing the node's NVLink here would describe hardware the run never touched.
hardware.interconnect_inter_node_u_reason: (U) single-node campaign only; multi-node scaling not measured
hardware.node_exclusivity_u_reason: (U) not captured; the node physically hosts 8 GPUs and this run used exactly 1, but whether the remaining devices were in use during the run was not recorded
hardware.hbm_bandwidth_bytes_s_u_reason: (U) not captured at run time and the vendor figure was not consulted for this declaration; without it the theoretical tier cannot be computed and roofline_efficiency MUST be null
hardware.dense_bf16_flops_per_s_u_reason: (U) not captured at run time and the vendor figure was not consulted for this declaration

notes.cpu_cores: A scheduler allocation, not the machine: the node reports 112 logical cores in total and the cluster QoS grants 12 per GPU, which is what this single-GPU run received. Under this image workload the host decodes and patchifies every request, so the 12 is a capacity input; host sampling during calibration peaked at 11.53 of them.
notes.gpus_per_node: The node hosts 8 H100s; this run was allocated 1. The other 7 are declared for topology, not because they served traffic.

model.image_tokens_min_u_reason: (U) lower clamp not captured from the preprocessor config; the worst case is bounded by image_tokens_max, which is declared
model.moe_experts_u_reason: (U) not applicable: this model is dense, so there is no expert count to report. The null is the architecture rather than a gap in what was captured.
model.moe_top_k_u_reason: (U) not applicable: a dense model routes every token through the same feed-forward block, so there is no router and no top-k to declare.

notes.mm_processor_cache_gb: Set to 0 deliberately, so every request pays host-side decode and patchify and the measurement carries preprocessing cost. With the cache on, a corpus that repeats media reports a speedup the production workload would never see, and nothing in the response reveals it.
notes.per_request_override_supported: False was verified, not assumed: this engine answers a per-request mm_processor_kwargs with HTTP 400, so the pixel budget above is the only one any client can get.

media_preprocessing.video_sampling_fps_u_reason: (U) no rate is declared because the deployment refuses video: the engine was started with a per-prompt video limit of 0 and answers a video part with HTTP 400. There is no sampling rate to report, not one that went unmeasured.
media_preprocessing.video_max_frames_u_reason: (U) the cap was looked for and is absent because no video reaches the preprocessor: the per-prompt video limit is 0, so the unbounded reading this null would otherwise carry -- unbounded frames, therefore unbounded context -- does not apply.

notes.engine_reported_kv_cache_tokens: Read from the engine log shipped in this bundle (job start 04:30, 429,952 tokens). The figure is not stable across boots of an identical configuration: an earlier start of the same sbatch on the same GPU reported 429,936, one 16-token KV block less, presumably because free memory after weight load moved slightly. Read it as +/- one block rather than exact, and never carry it between runs -- the bundle hashes the log beside this declaration, so a figure copied from a previous boot contradicts the evidence shipped with it.
notes.cold_start_to_ready_s: Measured from the engine first log line to Application startup complete, 04:30:19 to 04:31:01. This is a warm restart, not a first start: the log records "Directly load the compiled graph(s) for dynamic shape from the cache, took 2.280 s", so the torch.compile cache under VLLM_CACHE_ROOT was already populated by an earlier boot on this node. The same configuration's first start, with that cache empty, took 90 s. Size a cold rollout or an autoscaler that lands on a fresh node with the larger figure. Both are floors in any case: interpreter start and module import happen before anything is logged.
notes.framework_version: Operator-typed, but corroborated: the bundle environment capture reads the installed distribution versions, and on this deployment the benchmark client and the model server run in the same interpreter environment, so the vllm version it records is the one that served the requests rather than the harness host alone.

workload.duty_cycle_u_reason: (U) not captured: this is a closed-loop benchmark holding concurrency fixed per rung, so there is no duty cycle to observe -- the figure describes a production population, and inventing one here would let a load-generator artefact be read as user behaviour.
workload.output_tokens_per_request_u_reason: (U) not declared: output length was capped at 512 and left to real EOS rather than fixed, so the per-request distribution is an outcome of the corpus and is published per rung in the run layer, not forecast here.

notes.input_tokens_per_request: 722 is one observed datapoint, not a distribution: a single smoke request (a 960x720 PNG plus its question) against the live server returned prompt_tokens 722. The run's per-rung context means supersede it and are the figures to read; it is declared here because a workload layer carrying no input length at all cannot be composed with per-GPU figures measured anywhere else.

unmeasured_assumptions.impact_if_wrong: Without a roofline, a measured throughput far from the hardware's ceiling is indistinguishable from a healthy one, and the real bottleneck goes uninvestigated.
unmeasured_assumptions.cost_to_measure: Run `ascep size` against the declared hardware block; it needs bandwidth and FLOPs from the declaration, not another bench run.

unmeasured_assumptions.impact_if_wrong: A capacity decision made against the measured tier with no headroom leaves nothing for demand peaks; one made against an assumed headroom is policy dressed up as data.
unmeasured_assumptions.cost_to_measure: Declare the demand targets and run `ascep size`; the policy input is a capacity-planning decision, not a measurement.

unmeasured_assumptions.impact_if_wrong: A single topology says nothing about scaling efficiency, and extrapolating it to a node count this run never measured can halve or double a GPU order.
unmeasured_assumptions.cost_to_measure: Repeat the ladder at each tensor-parallel and pipeline-parallel degree of interest and fill one row per topology.

unmeasured_assumptions.impact_if_wrong: Server-reported usage goes unchecked, so an engine that miscounts tokens inflates every tokens-per-second figure in this report.
unmeasured_assumptions.cost_to_measure: Count prompts and outputs locally with the served model's own tokenizer, as chapter 4.7.1 requires; bench ships no tokenizer to do it.

unmeasured_assumptions.field: capacity_tiers.*.binding_constraint (weights and KV floors not evaluated)
unmeasured_assumptions.impact_if_wrong: The named constraint is the floor observed under the declared gates. A weights or KV floor lower than it would not have been seen, so a deployment whose true floor is KV at another context length is still sized against the wrong resource, and the shortfall appears only in production.
unmeasured_assumptions.cost_to_measure: Inspect engine-reported KV cache occupancy and memory headroom on the serving host during the run, and repeat the ladder at longer context lengths; latency at one context length cannot decide the weights or KV floors.

unmeasured_assumptions.impact_if_wrong: Without utilization, a rung that failed its gates because the GPU was saturated is indistinguishable from one that failed because the client, the network or another tenant was, and the ladder's boundary gets attributed to the wrong component.
unmeasured_assumptions.cost_to_measure: Sample the serving host during each window -- nvidia-smi, DCGM, or the engine's own metrics endpoint -- and align the series to the window timestamps in the bundle; a load generator cannot see it over HTTP.

unmeasured_assumptions.impact_if_wrong: Throughput moves by tens of percent between engine releases, so a report without the version cannot be compared with another run of the same model on the same hardware -- which is most of what these reports get used for.
unmeasured_assumptions.cost_to_measure: Read it from the serving host or the container image and record it; `/v1/models` does not carry it, so bench cannot ask.

unmeasured_assumptions.field: figures published below the section 4.3 advisory sample floor: e2e_p95_s at concurrency 1, ttft_p95_s at concurrency 1, e2e_p95_s at concurrency 2, ttft_p95_s at concurrency 2, e2e_p95_s at concurrency 4, e2e_p99_s at concurrency 4, itl_p95_s at concurrency 4, ttft_p95_s at concurrency 4, ttft_p99_s at concurrency 4, e2e_p99_s at concurrency 8, ttft_p99_s at concurrency 8, e2e_p99_s at concurrency 16, ttft_p99_s at concurrency 16
unmeasured_assumptions.impact_if_wrong: These percentiles are computed from enough samples to report but not enough to be stable: a single straggler moves them, so a tier boundary that turns on one of them can flip between two runs of the same config.
unmeasured_assumptions.cost_to_measure: Lengthen the window or raise the repetition count until the tail percentile clears its advisory floor; the sample count, not the estimator, is the limit.
